venues.name: Boulder Theater

seatingFormat.note: Reviewers describe a multi-tier main floor (standing near the stage and/or reserved rows depending on the show) plus a balcony with fixed seats; GA shows are commonly split between standing on the floor and sitting in the balcony. Layout varies per event. Official site pages for the layout were not retrievable.

agePolicy.text: AXS venue page says shows are generally all ages unless an event states otherwise, with guests under 15 needing an adult. Varies by show, so check each listing.

doors.text: No standard doors time found. Box office opens about 90 minutes before doors on event nights; the attached lounge opens an hour before doors.

parking.summary: No venue lot. Street parking downtown (AXS says typically free after 7 pm) plus several nearby garages. A community reviewer says downtown parking can be tough but street spots are usually findable; another reported a ticket for parking in the disabled space out front.

transit.summary: AXS notes RTD bus stops downtown near the theater. Specific routes not verified.

policies.bag: AXS says large bags and containers are prohibited; full official bag rules not retrieved.
policies.other: Official site links to separate FAQ, Directions & Parking and Accessibility pages that could not be opened; verify there.

accessibility.summary: A venue directory says ADA accessibility is offered with accessible seating requested via the box office. One older Tripadvisor reviewer said it was not wheelchair friendly despite ADA compliance (community-reported, 2016-2018 era). Contact box office (303-786-7030) before attending.

area.summary: Downtown Boulder at 2032 14th St, in a walkable area with things to do before and after shows. A reviewer says shows tend to end early, around 11:30 pm.

sound.summary: Reviewers consistently praise sound as crisp from floor, seats and balcony, and say sightlines are good thanks to the tiered floor. Some find the reserved-row chairs cramped.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Good sound and sightlines from most spots, including the tiered floor.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Balcony seating is reportedly first come, first served at GA shows, so arriving early matters for front-row balcony.
Reviewers mention long security lines and crowded lobby/restrooms at busy shows; allow extra entry time.
Large bags are not allowed, so travel light.
Some reviewers call the building dated or worn and mention high ticket fees.

venues.notes: Official bouldertheater.com FAQ was unreachable (redirects to z2ent.com page which lacks details). Capacity 850 is from AXS (described as seats) and a directory; actual capacity varies by configuration. Tripadvisor reviews seen were mostly 2016-2018.

venues.name: Fox Theatre

seatingFormat.note: Standing room; bench seating along the outer walls is first come, first served. Guests who cannot stand all show can request accommodation in advance by emailing the address on the FAQ.

agePolicy.text: 21+ unless noted. 'AA' means all ages (under 15 needs a parent) and 'LAA' means limited all ages with few tickets. Varies by show.

doors.text: Specific doors time not stated. Box office opens at 6pm on show nights only.

parking.summary: No parking details on the official FAQ. The venue sits on University Hill near CU; a Directions & Parking page exists on the Z2 site but could not be read.

policies.bag: A listing says backpacks are banned; the official FAQ did not mention bags.
policies.reentry: Guests who step out to smoke may re-enter; general re-entry rules not stated.
policies.other: Photo ID (license or passport) required for 21+ shows and for ticket pickup. No smoking inside, marijuana included. Listing also reports vaping, weapons and outside food/alcohol are banned.

accessibility.summary: No general accessibility info on the FAQ; physical-condition accommodations are arranged by emailing the venue in advance. Z2 site links to an Accessibility page that could not be read.

area.summary: 1135 13th St on University Hill, a commercial and nightlife district across from the CU campus.

sound.summary: No consistent sound or sightline reports found. With a standing crowd, view depends on where you stand.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Intimate, standing-room club of roughly 600 people.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Most shows are 21+; check the AA/LAA marker and bring a valid photo ID.
Mostly standing with limited first-come bench seating, so plan for a long time on your feet.
Leave the backpack at home (reported ban).

venues.notes: Capacity: official FAQ 625; Wikipedia says seating 'just over 600', directory says about 600. Parking, transit and sound could not be verified from sources.

venues.name: Chautauqua Auditorium

seatingFormat.note: Padded wooden-backed opera seats in lettered reserved sections, plus a general admission area (some benches remain). Wheelchair spots must be selected at purchase.

agePolicy.text: All ages unless stated. Under 2 free on a lap; over 2 needs a ticket. Check each event.

doors.text: No doors time on FAQ; listings show start time only. Shuttle begins about 90 minutes before showtime.

parking.summary: Parking on the grounds is very limited. Free curbside first-come parking on the south side of Baseline Rd (paid via pay stations/ParkMobile in summer evenings per Colorado Music Festival). The free HOP 2 Chautauqua shuttle is encouraged; suggested lots include 27th Way Park-n-Ride, New Vista High School (concert nights) and downtown garages. City paid parking at Chautauqua is $2.50/hour on weekends and summer holidays.

transit.summary: Free HOP 2 Chautauqua shuttle on Auditorium concert nights: starts 90 min before showtime, buses roughly every 15-20 min, main stop at the RTD station at 14th & Walnut, with stops along Broadway; returns wait after the show. Rideshare to the Dining Hall is another option. Note the separate city Park-to-Park shuttle is weekends only in summer and ended for 2026.

policies.bag: Bags must fit under your seat (about 12x16x12 in or smaller); all bags inspected. Coolers, picnic baskets, framed packs and large umbrellas not allowed.
policies.other: Outside food and drink prohibited except water. Beer, wine and soft drinks sold on site.

accessibility.summary: ADA access via the south entrance, reserved wheelchair spots and GA accessible seating, designated accessible parking, accessible shuttle pickup, and FM assistive listening with free receivers.

area.summary: At 900 Baseline Rd at the foot of the Flatirons. The auditorium has no heating or air conditioning and stays about as warm or cool as outdoors; the FAQ suggests a jacket for Sept/Oct shows. Season is roughly May to early autumn (sources differ: May-Oct vs May-Sept).

sound.summary: The all-wood hall has long been noted for strong natural acoustics, and the Colorado Music Festival chose it for its reverberation.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Historic wooden hall with notable natural acoustics.
Free shuttle on concert nights eases the parking problem and offers return service.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Parking is limited and the venue urges using the shuttle, carpooling or biking.
No heating or cooling; dress for outdoor temperatures, especially in September/October.
Small bags only (must fit under the seat) and bags are inspected.

venues.notes: Capacity 1,300 comes only from Cinema Treasures (secondary); official FAQ gives no number. Season length conflicts between sources. HOP page text appears to be an older 2021-era URL; confirm current shuttle details. No community reviews were gathered for sound beyond history sources.

venues.name: Roots Music Project

seatingFormat.note: Not stated. Site describes a warehouse venue with a full stage and bar; seating arrangement varies by event, unverified.

agePolicy.text: No venue-wide policy found. Some events are described as all ages; check each event listing.

doors.text: Varies by event; examples on the site include doors at 7pm with show at 8pm.

parking.summary: A county arts listing says parking is available around the warehouse plus free street parking. Not verified by the venue.

policies.other: Tickets sold through the venue's ticketing site (RMPtix.com). Full-service bar on site, seasonal biergarten.

area.summary: Warehouse space at 4747 Pearl St, Suite V3A, Boulder, a nonprofit founded in 2019 that books mostly Americana and also DJ nights.

sound.summary: Venue advertises a state-of-the-art lighting and sound system; no independent sound reports found.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Small nonprofit room with a relaxed, supportive atmosphere per a county arts listing, and a full bar.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Age rules and doors times vary by event; read each listing before buying.

venues.notes: Capacity 250 appears in a promotional post on the homepage, not a dedicated FAQ. The county arts listing shows a Broomfield address, conflicting with the venue's 4747 Pearl St, Boulder address. A third-party aggregator page listing a 75-space lot and many policies looked templated (555 phone numbers) and was deliberately not used. Official FAQ unreachable.

venues.name: Hi-Dive

seatingFormat.note: Small club where you can stand a few feet from the band, per a local guide. Seating not described; treat as standing.

agePolicy.text: Not on the official homepage. A single third-party aggregator says generally 21+ with rare all-ages shows and ID required; weak source, verify per show.

policies.other: Aggregator says ID and the purchasing card are needed for will-call; unverified.

area.summary: 7 S Broadway, Denver, in the Baker neighborhood. Musician-owned club open since 2003.

sound.summary: Owners upgraded the sound system after buying the club (Westword), and a youth music site says it is known for sound quality.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Long-running local rock club that has hosted rising acts before they broke big, with a no-frills interior.
Intimate room with close views of bands and cheap drinks per a local guide.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Small space: expect crowding at popular shows; one guide calls the restrooms poor.
Confirm age policy and doors with the venue; none verified from official pages.

venues.notes: Official hi-dive.com homepage lists no capacity, age, parking or accessibility; FAQ page was unreachable. Westword says only that it is among venues under 500 capacity. Address conflict: homepage says 7 S Broadway; Youth on Record lists 1301 W 10th Ave, treated as outdated. Westword article is older than its 'last year' purchase wording suggests.
